brief.1979_q3_stagflation.desc: Staff outlook under three policy scenarios: tightening, holding, or easing from the current stance. Elevated inflation and energy prices dominate the near-term path.

brief.2008_q4_crisis.desc: Staff outlook under three policy scenarios as credit markets seize. A deflationary demand collapse is the dominant near-term risk; the toolkit is untested at the zero lower bound.

brief.2008_q4_crisis.lower.name: Lower — Emergency Easing

brief.2020_q1_pandemic.desc: Staff outlook under three policy scenarios as the pandemic halts activity. Simultaneous demand and supply disruption; unemployment is projected to spike at unprecedented speed.
brief.2020_q1_pandemic.raise.name: Raise — Preempt Supply Inflation
brief.2020_q1_pandemic.hold.name: Hold — Assess Incoming Data

evt.oil_shock.title: Oil Shock
evt.oil_shock.desc: Crude prices spike as overseas tensions flare. The supply shock will push headline inflation up regardless of what you do.
tech.applied.omo.name: Open Market Operations
tech.applied.omo.desc: Buying and selling government securities to steer the policy rate.
tech.applied.qe.name: Large-Scale Asset Purchases
tech.applied.qe.desc: Balance-sheet policy for when the policy rate is pinned at the lower bound.

scen.1979_stagflation.name: Late-1970s Stagflation
scen.1979_stagflation.desc: August 1979: inflation runs above 11% and institutional credibility is shredded. Tighten aggressively enough to break expectations — without breaking the economy.
scen.recovery_test.name: Recovery Mode Test Fixture
scen.recovery_test.desc: Test-only scenario with credibility above anchor_threshold so engine tests can exercise the SPEC-GUIDE-1 recovery path through Session.advance() without first having to traverse drift mode.
scen.2008_gfc.name: 2008 Global Financial Crisis
scen.2008_gfc.desc: September 2008: a sudden credit freeze and collapsing demand threaten a deflationary spiral. Credibility is solid but the toolkit is untested at the zero lower bound.
scen.covid_2020.name: 2020 Pandemic Shock
scen.covid_2020.desc: March 2020: simultaneous demand collapse and supply disruption. Low inflation and high credibility give room to act — but the speed and scale of the shock are unprecedented.
replay.1979_chair_tightening.name: 1979 Chair Tightening
replay.1979_chair_tightening.desc: The 1979-1986 late-stagflation disinflation strategy: ramp the fed funds rate to ~19% by mid-1981, then ease as inflation breaks. A canned strategy for testing the engine end-to-end.
comm.fomc_1979.name: Federal Open Market Committee (1979)
comm.fomc_1979.desc: The FOMC as constituted in August 1979. A mix of hawks, doves, and centrists across the Board and regional banks.

doctrine.inflation_targeting.name: Inflation Targeting
doctrine.inflation_targeting.desc: A public commitment to a numeric inflation target as the primary objective. Strengthens institutional credibility while in force; abandoning it carries reputational consequences.

hearing.confirmation.name: Confirmation Hearing
hearing.confirmation.desc: Answer the Senate Banking Committee's questions. Your answers will shape the starting scenario and your initial institutional standing.
hearing.q.inflation_priority.text: Chair-designate, the Federal Reserve's dual mandate asks you to balance price stability with maximum employment. In your view, which deserves priority when they conflict?
hearing.a.inflation_strict.text: Price stability is the precondition for sustainable employment. I will act decisively to anchor inflation expectations.
hearing.a.inflation_balanced.text: Both objectives are co-equal. I will not sacrifice one for the other without exhausting intermediate options.
hearing.a.inflation_dovish.text: Employment is the lived experience of millions of families. I will exercise patience before imposing unnecessary tightening.
hearing.q.institutional_posture.text: How do you view the Federal Reserve's relationship with the elected government? Should the central bank coordinate its policy with the administration's fiscal objectives?
hearing.a.posture_independent.text: The Fed's independence from short-term political pressure is what makes our inflation commitment credible. I intend to preserve that.
hearing.a.posture_cooperative.text: Coordination between monetary and fiscal authorities, within each institution's mandate, produces better macro outcomes than operating at cross-purposes.
hearing.q.crisis_response.text: Looking at the current macroeconomic environment, how would you characterize the primary risk, and what is your preferred first-response framework?
hearing.a.crisis_orthodox.text: The primary risk is entrenched inflation expectations. Conventional rate policy remains the right tool; I am prepared to accept near-term output costs.
hearing.a.crisis_activist.text: The situation calls for an active, broad toolkit — including balance-sheet measures — deployed swiftly before conditions deteriorate further.
hearing.a.crisis_pragmatic.text: I will assess the data as it arrives and choose instruments proportionate to the threat. Flexibility is a virtue, not a vice.
trait.hawkish_lean.name: Inflation Hawk
trait.hawkish_lean.desc: Consistently applies upward pressure on the preferred rate; prioritizes price stability over output.
trait.dovish_lean.name: Labor Dove
trait.dovish_lean.desc: Consistently applies downward pressure on the preferred rate; emphasizes employment in the dual mandate.
trait.principled_dissenter.name: Principled Dissenter
trait.principled_dissenter.desc: Narrows the band of acceptable proposals; more likely to dissent when the proposed rate diverges from their own view.
trait.ag_hawk.name: Agricultural Hawk
trait.ag_hawk.desc: Sensitive to agricultural commodity prices; will press for tighter policy if food prices surge (dormant until sectoral series available).
trait.manufacturing_dove.name: Manufacturing Dove
trait.manufacturing_dove.desc: Sensitive to manufacturing employment; advocates easier policy when factory hiring weakens (dormant until sectoral series available).
ui.start.title: MANDATE
ui.start.subtitle: Choose a starting scenario, or face the Senate first.
ui.mandate.label: Mandate
ui.doctrine.heading: Doctrine
doctrine.dot_plot.name: Dot Plot
doctrine.dot_plot.desc: Publish each member's preferred rate after every meeting. Transparency strengthens anchoring while the committee agrees; a visibly divided committee pays a credibility cost proportional to the spread.
doctrine.gradualism.name: Gradualism
doctrine.gradualism.desc: Commit to moving the policy rate in small, well-telegraphed steps. Markets reward the predictability with a standing credibility bonus — but abandoning the commitment mid-cycle is costly.
ui.shell.desk.heading: The Desk
ui.institution.heading: The Institution
ui.institution.subtitle: Build the organization. Staff the divisions that turn raw data into a clear view.
ui.legacy.heading: Legacy
ui.legacy.subtitle: Your record is the institution you leave behind.
division.research.name: Research & Statistics
division.research.desc: Turns raw data into forecasts. A strong head sharpens the staff briefing and lifts the data fog.
division.monetary_affairs.name: Monetary Affairs
division.monetary_affairs.desc: Designs and executes policy implementation. Improves the precision of the committee's deliberations.
division.financial_stability.name: Financial Stability
division.financial_stability.desc: Watches fragility build across the financial network and flags systemic risk before it spreads.
division.supervision.name: Supervision & Regulation
division.supervision.desc: Oversees the banks. Strong supervision hardens the system but makes enemies among institutions.
division.international.name: International Finance
division.international.desc: Tracks exchange rates, capital flows, and peer central banks whose moves wash ashore.
division.rbops.name: Reserve Bank Operations & Payment Systems
division.rbops.desc: Keeps the plumbing running — payment rails, settlement, and operational resilience. A steady hand here makes the system harder to break.
division.consumer_community.name: Consumer & Community Affairs
division.consumer_community.desc: Consumer protection and community reinvestment. A strong record buys goodwill on Capitol Hill.
division.legal.name: Legal
division.legal.desc: Defends the Fed's authority. Sound legal footing lowers the political cost of contested actions.
division.coo.name: Office of the COO
division.coo.desc: Runs the institution day to day. An effective COO lowers the cost of every other division and lifts the whole org.
division.oig.name: Office of Inspector General
division.oig.desc: Independent oversight reporting to the Chair. Strong internal audit heads off scandal before it reaches the press.
ui.institution.deferred_asset_warning: The Fed is operating at a loss — a deferred asset is accruing and Congress is asking questions.
ui.crisis.banner: Financial crisis underway — credit is seizing and the real economy is taking the hit.
ui.escalations.heading: On your desk
ui.escalations.subtitle: Matters your division heads have escalated for a decision.
ui.escalations.empty: Nothing awaiting your decision. The institution is running itself — for now.
ui.persuasion.legend: Each member weighs inflation and unemployment differently in their own reaction function — those who fear inflation most want higher rates. Spend Chair capital to widen a member's tolerance and win their assent.
evt.regional_bank_distress.title: Regional bank under strain
evt.regional_bank_distress.desc: Supervision flags a mid-size bank with thinning capital and souring loans. Left alone it could fail and rattle the system.
evt.regional_bank_distress.opt.intervene: Order corrective action and shore it up
evt.staff_poached.title: Wall Street comes calling
evt.staff_poached.desc: A major bank is dangling a fortune in front of one of your division heads. Lose them and you lose institutional memory.
evt.staff_poached.opt.counter: Make the case to stay (spend budget on retention)
evt.staff_poached.opt.let_go: Wish them well and let them walk
evt.congressional_letter.title: A pointed letter from the Hill
evt.congressional_letter.desc: A bloc of senators demands you explain the inflation path and threatens hearings if you don't bend.
evt.congressional_letter.opt.defend: Defend the Fed's independence, firmly and publicly
evt.congressional_letter.opt.accommodate: Strike a conciliatory tone and buy goodwill
evt.market_jitters.title: Markets are jittery
evt.market_jitters.desc: Volatility is spiking and traders are hunting for a signal from you. A word now moves expectations.
evt.market_jitters.opt.stay_silent: Say nothing and let it settle
evt.fiscal_stimulus.title: The government opens the spigot
evt.fiscal_stimulus.desc: A large stimulus package is announced. It will heat the economy — and complicate your job.
evt.fiscal_stimulus.opt.lean_against: Signal you'll lean against the overheating
evt.fiscal_stimulus.opt.accommodate: Hold your tone and avoid a public clash
evt.bank_lobby.title: The banks push back
evt.bank_lobby.desc: Industry lobbyists are pressing hard against your supervisory stance, working their allies in Congress.
evt.bank_lobby.opt.hold_firm: Hold the line on tough supervision
evt.bank_lobby.opt.ease: Ease the stance and bank the goodwill
evt.foreign_crisis.title: A crisis washes ashore
evt.foreign_crisis.desc: A foreign financial crisis is spilling into dollar markets. International Finance wants to know your posture.
evt.foreign_crisis.opt.swap_lines: Open swap lines and backstop the system
evt.foreign_crisis.opt.stand_back: Stand back — it's not our fire to fight
evt.deferred_asset_press.title: The press smells a loss
evt.deferred_asset_press.desc: Reporters have noticed the Fed is remitting nothing to Treasury and are framing it as a taxpayer cost.
evt.deferred_asset_press.opt.explain: Explain the accounting plainly and own it
evt.deferred_asset_press.opt.deflect: Decline to engage with the framing
